review.summary: Round 12 reviews the whole TASK-069A branch at the round-11 fix commit. All four round-11 findings are verified fixed: the redirect host is always returned and shown only for non-loopback redirects, consistently in ADR-015, TASK-069E and TASK-069L; the loopback sentence refers to the notice; short lines are rewrapped; and the connections response uses camelCase JSON keys matching existing schemas. A CommonMark render shows the changed paragraphs correctly. Scope is still documentation-only. likec4@1.60.0 validate passes and the committed PNGs are byte-identical to a fresh export with the README command; relative links and anchors resolve; the review records validate. One new info finding: TASK-069K and TASK-069M still spell the client identifier in snake_case.

findings.summary: The change-set review detail and the Metrics AI panel still name the client identifier client_id, while the connections API and UI now use clientId.
findings.rationale: TASK-069K's detail response and TASK-069M's display and tests were not updated with the camelCase rename, so an implementer could emit a snake_case JSON key there.
findings.recommendation: Use clientId in TASK-069K and TASK-069M, or state once in TASK-069K that the detail's JSON keys are camelCase like the rest of /api/v1.

prior_finding_dispositions.rationale: TASK-069E now always returns the redirect host in URL form and the page shows it only when the loopback flag is false, with matching tests in TASK-069E and TASK-069L and agreement with ADR-015.
ADR-015 now says a loopback host only identifies a program on the user's own machine, so the page shows the loopback notice instead.
The cited lines in ADR-015, TASK-069K and TASK-069M are rewrapped; rendering is correct.

TASK-069F now lists camelCase JSON keys for the connections response, matching the existing time-field naming in the predictions schemas, keeps snake_case for columns and the path parameter, and TASK-069L uses the same keys.
